about.title: The classic rolled bamboo fence

body.p: Our natural bamboo fence roll is made from round yellow bamboo canes, laid side by side and bound with galvanised iron wire. Because the canes are wired rather than fixed into a frame, the screen rolls up for compact shipping and unrolls on site to follow a fence line, a balcony railing or a gentle curve. It is what most buyers mean by a bamboo screening roll, and it suits garden boundaries, cladding for chain-link, wooden or concrete fences, balconies and terraces, garden-centre ranges and landscaping projects.

body.h3: Three cane grades, plus giant canes

body.p: Thinner 14–20 mm canes make a lighter, more economical roll; 20–30 mm is the everyday grade; 30–35 mm gives a heavier, more solid look. For statement projects we also make a giant version with 35–40 or 40–50 mm canes, bound with wire, a bamboo pole or nylon wire. A varnish lacquer finish is available as an option for a smoother, more finished surface.

Before loading, our QC team measures the moisture content of the canes — recent checks read between 7.8% and 11.9% — and checks cane diameters with a tape against the order. Roll sizes from 100 × 180 cm up to 250 × 180 cm are photographed before packing, so you see what goes into the container.

faq.q: What sizes does the natural bamboo fence roll come in?
faq.a: Seven standard sizes from 1.0 × 2.5 m to 2.5 × 2.5 m (height × width). The popular 6 ft bamboo fence roll is our 1.8 m height, in 1.8 m or 2.5 m widths. Other heights and widths are made to order.

faq.q: How much fits in a 40HC container?
faq.a: It depends on the cane grade: about 2,400 m² of 14–20 mm, 2,300 m² of 20–30 mm or 2,100 m² of 30–35 mm per 40HC. The exact number of rolls depends on your size mix and packing, so we calculate it for each order.

faq.q: How is a bamboo fence roll installed?
faq.a: Unroll it against an existing fence, wall, railing or chain-link and fix it with wire ties or screws through the wire. For a free-standing fence, fix the roll to timber posts and rails. No special tools are needed.

faq.q: Will the natural colour change outdoors?
faq.a: Yes, gradually. Like any untreated natural material, bamboo slowly weathers to a softer, greyer tone in sun and rain. The varnish lacquer option adds a protective surface layer; for a darker look from the start, see our natural black or carbonized rolls.

about.title: Colour that goes all the way through

body.p: Carbonized bamboo is bamboo that has been heat-treated. The process darkens the cane from its natural yellow to a brown or deeper tone, and because it is heat rather than a coating, the colour runs through the whole cane. A knock, a scratch or a freshly cut end shows the same colour as the surface.

After carbonizing, the canes are finished with varnish lacquer and wired into rolls with galvanised wire, so the fence installs exactly like our natural bamboo fence roll. Both grades come in the same seven roll sizes as our other round rolls, from 1.0 × 2.5 m to 2.5 × 2.5 m, so carbonized can join a mixed container of natural and black rolls without changing your size range.

about.title: A stronger bamboo, in a finished frame

body.p: Tonkin bamboo is one of the strongest and most flexible bamboo species, with long, straight poles that keep an even diameter. It is also naturally bitter, which makes it less attractive to insects. We only use poles that have grown for three years or more, so the cane has had time to harden. Like all bamboo, Tonkin is a fast-growing, renewable plant that regrows after harvesting.

Rather than wiring the poles into a roll, we set them in a wood frame to make a rigid screen. The standard screen measures 120 cm wide, 180 cm high and 5 cm thick, and weighs 22 kg net — a solid, finished panel that fixes straight to posts or a wall.
The natural version keeps Tonkin's pale straw colour. The carbonized version is heat-treated for a warmer brown tone that runs through the cane.

Our bamboo fence rolls are flexible, light and fast to unroll over an existing fence. The Tonkin screen is heavier and framed, so it stands on its own between posts and gives a more architectural, premium result. Each screen is packed in plastic foam on a pallet to protect the frame in transit.

about.title: A Japanese accent screen

body.p: In Japanese gardens, a sode-gaki or sleeve fence is a short screen that projects from a building, a wall or a gate, like a sleeve from a kimono. It does not enclose a space; it frames a view, hides something functional or gives a planting group a backdrop.

Our Sode-gaki bamboo sleeve fence is made from natural yellow bamboo. A tall bamboo post forms one side, a curved lattice top sweeps away from it, and upright canes fill the panel below. The panel is 90 mm thick and comes in four sizes, from a compact 45 × 120 cm (18 × 48 in) to 90 × 170 cm (36 × 68 in). Like all our bamboo, it is renewable and made without pesticides, formaldehyde or toxic glues.

about.title: An open, sculptural Japanese fence

body.p: Koetsu-gaki is a traditional Japanese bamboo fence style named after Koetsu-ji temple in Kyoto. Its signature is a long top rail that curves down from a post, over an open lattice of crossed bamboo. It is a fence to look at and through, not a screen to hide behind.

Our Koetsu-gaki bamboo wing fence is made from natural yellow bamboo. A bamboo post anchors one end, the curved top rail sweeps away from it, and split bamboo forms an open diamond lattice below. The panel is 90 mm thick and comes in six sizes, from a 60 × 60 cm (24 × 24 in) accent to a 200 × 90 cm (79 × 36 in) low run.
